answer: In an agent economy coordinating nectar deliveries across a mesa, every bidding identity must lock $100 in escrow for the full delivery window. The ledger prevents the same funds from backing multiple identities, so creating a ripple of 1,000 fake agents requires locking $100,000. This does not prove the agents have different owners; it makes each additional active identity consume scarce capital, imposing financing costs on the attacker.
